title: Above, Below, Where'er I Gaze
description: Above, Below, Where'er I Gaze in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 116 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Omnipresence of God”, where the book credits them to Montgomery's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-bove, be-low, wher-e'er I gaze, Thy gui-ding fin-ger, Lord, I view, Traced in the mid-night plan-ets' blaze, Or glist'n-ing in the morn-ing dew: What-e'er is beau-ti-ful or fair, Is but thine own re-flec-tion there.

lines: Thy guiding finger, Lord, I view,
Traced in the midnight planets' blaze,
Or glist'ning in the morning dew:
Is but thine own reflection there.
And when the radiant orb of light
Hath tipped the mountain tops with gold
Smote with the blaze, my weary sight
Shrinks from the wonders I behold;
That ray of glory, bright and fair,
Is but thy living shadow there.
Thine is the silent noon of night,
The twilight eve, the dewy morn;
Thy hands have fashioned to adorn.
Thy glory walks in every sphere,
And all things whisper, "God is here."

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
